nodes.name: Carbonization of ZIF-8
nodes.procedure: The nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) support is derived from the carbonization of ZIF-8 at 600 °C, at which the C-H, N-H, and C-N bonds in the structure of ZIF-8 are disrupted and reorganized.
nodes.source_text: the nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) support is derived from the carbonization of ZIF-8 at 600 °C

nodes.name: Copyrolysis of Ni catalyst
nodes.procedure: NC, urea, and nickel nitrate were homogeneously mixed and calcined at 900 °C to obtain a Ni-N5-C catalyst. During the pyrolysis process, urea causes nitrogen doping and acts as a blowing agent to create a large number of internal voids in the carbon support.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms abundant mesopores and absence of nanoparticles in the Ni-N5-C catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure S4) ... demonstrate the presence of abundant mesopores in the Ni-N5-C catalyst, while nanoparticles are absent.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms monatomic dispersion of Ni atoms uniformly distributed in the carbon substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM was applied to confirm the existence of the form of Ni ... indicating a uniform population of Ni atoms (Figure 1e).

properties.description: Line profile showing atomic distance between metal centers.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows homogeneously dispersed Ni species throughout the catalyst architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images verify the homogeneously dispersed Ni species over the entire architecture (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD reveals carbon phases (002) and (100) but no peaks for Ni or Zn, suggesting atomically dispersed Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni-N5-C reveals two peaks at ~24.72 and ~43.52 ... absence of peaks for Ni and Zn in the XRD pattern of the sample indicates the absence of metal and oxide crystals

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p3/2 peak between Ni2+ and Ni0, and a Metal-N peak at 399.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p3/2 peak lies between those of Ni2+ and Ni0. ... The deconvoluted N 1s spectra of Ni-N5-C contain a metal-N peak at 399.5 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows a valence state between Ni foil and NiO2 (0 to +2). In situ XANES under magnetic field shows Ni-N bond shortening upon *COOH adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pre-edge of Ni-N5-C and Ni-N5-C-M ... is between Ni foil and NiO2, revealing that the valence state of the Ni atom is between 0 and +2 (Figure 2a) ... shortening increases the overlap between Ni and ligand orbitals ... as the *COOH intermediate adsorbs

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows a Ni-N path at ~1.4 A and no Ni-Ni path, indicating Ni is coordinated to five N atoms in a square pyramidal geometry.
nodes.evidence_snippet: main peak at ~1.4 A is observed, attributed to the typical Ni-N scattering path, while the Ni-Ni peak at ~2.2 A is not observed ... Ni atom coordinates to five N atoms, forming a square pyramidal geometry

visual_evidence.name: Faradaic Efficiency vs Current Density Chart

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows a g value of 2.0046, indicating negligible spin-orbit coupling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurement shows that the Ni-N5-C catalyst exhibits a g value of 2.0046

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ EIS reveals potential-dependent charge transfer resistance changes; a 2T magnetic field increases resistance at -1.1V vs RHE due to CO2RR onset slowing the HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a larger diameter for the arc appears suddenly at -1.1 V vs. RHE, illustrating the switch of reaction kinetics entering the HER and the CO2RR region.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen absorption-desorption isotherms show a substantial BET area of 1336.68 m2 g−1 and indicate both micro- and mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nitrogen absorption-desorption isotherms further indicate that the obtained Ni-N5-C catalyst possesses both micro- and mesopores and a substantial Brunner-Emmet-Teller (BET) area of 1336.68 m2·g−1 ... (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge spectra show 'white-line' features at 852.2 and 869.6 eV that decrease with increasing magnetic field strength, reflecting surface electronic structure changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni L-edge spectrum is derived from the Ni 2p to 3d electron transition ... two prominent "white-line" features at 852.2 and 869.6 eV in the Ni L-edge spectra steadily decrease with the increase of the applied magnetic field strength.
